facts.fact_text: Both applicants are political activists and opposition leaders.
On 5 December 2011 the applicants took part in a public demonstration (a meeting) at Chistyye Prudy, Moscow.
The public demonstration on 5 December 2011 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged State Duma elections.
After the demonstration on 5 December 2011, the applicants were arrested.
Both applicants were arrested at about 8.45 p.m. on 5 December 2011.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, at the material time, provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of their official duties related to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the performance by them of their official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between 500 and 1,000 Russian roubles or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

Article 20.2(2) of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, at the material time, provided that breaches of the established procedure for the conduct of public gatherings, meetings, demonstrations, marches or pickets shall be punishable by an administrative fine of between 1,000 and 2,000 Russian roubles for the organisers, and between 500 and 1,000 Russian roubles for the participants.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, at the material time, provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of their official duties related to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the performance by them of their official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between 500 and 1,000 Russian roubles or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.
The demonstration on 5 December 2011 had been duly authorised by the mayor of Moscow.
The number of participants at the meeting on 5 December 2011 was estimated between 5,000 and 10,000.
According to the applicants, no one in the surrounded group put up any resistance.
The applicants claimed that they obeyed the police and followed them to the police bus.
According to the Government, the marchers pushed through the police cordon at the crossroads of Pushechnaya and Rozhdestvenka Streets and went on.
According to the Government, the marchers ignored the repeated demands of the police to stop and thereby prevented the police from carrying out their mission of securing public order.

The Tverskoy District Court of Moscow held that during his arrest the first applicant, in reply to an invitation to proceed to the police bus for the issuing of an administrative offence report, began to push away police officers I. and F., trying to cause panic among people, thereby manifesting his refusal to comply with the lawful orders of the police and preventing them from carrying out their duties, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants' request to see their lawyers at the Severnoye Izmaylovo District police station was refused.
The applicants were not allowed to make a phone call to their families at the Severnoye Izmaylovo District police station.
At the Vostochnyy District police station the applicants requested to see a lawyer and to make a phone call, but this was refused.
At the Kitay-Gorod District police station the applicants requested permission to see their lawyers and to telephone their families, but their requests were refused.
The Justice of the Peace refused to entertain the first applicant's complaints concerning the lack of access to a lawyer after his arrest.
The Justice of the Peace refused to entertain the first applicant's complaints concerning the refusal of a statutory phone call after the arrest.
The Justice of the Peace refused to entertain the first applicant's complaints concerning the inhuman and degrading conditions of transfer and of detention at the Kitay-Gorod District police station.
